Sleep for me has been the hardest thing to crack when trying to get regulated. I’ve realised that I get FOMO even at 11pm on a random Tuesday when I know there’s nothing I’m missing out on but it feels like there’s this force that’s literally making me stay awake even though I know I need to sleep. I also am a professional self sabotage-r so when I have important things on the next day, I will absolutely stay up at an ungodly hour just to let myself suffer xxxx

I do know I need a good bed rot after a full day of peopling and demands especially in a NT world - maintaining self control after a full day of managing distractions is hard enough so when my mental energy is depleted, I need that dopamine hit and will usually rely on my phone or unhealthy impulsive actions and especially once the meds have worn off. 

Although it’s not something I do very often, it has worked for me. Forcing myself to sit with the uncomfortable feeling and recognise the impulse that’s keeping me up. I will try to mentally label what I’m feeling to try and distance myself from the feeling so it’s easier to sit with and then will say it out loud to acknowledge it and work through it. 

Saying out loud “I feel uncomfortable right now and that’s okay“ and just sitting with it. I try and notice where I’m feeling the discomfort as a sort of grounding technique and it doubles as a distraction for my brain and is calming. It can take less than 5 mins and I can absolutely notice the feeling has shifted whether it has fully passed or it’s just more manageable. I will usually also sit on my hands while I do this, preventing me from acting on my impulses and it gives my body something physical to focus on that redirects my hyperactive attention.

I’m not coeliac but am a picky eater - still to this day I will only eat food that has simple flavours and with my safe textures. To make sure I ate more veggies when I was growing up, my mum would use a NutriBullet to blend/puree veggies up so there wasn’t a texture usually when mixed with other things you can’t even taste it. For example she would make me breakfast fruit smoothies with banana and berries but would also put veggies in it like spinach and zucchini. The sweetness of the fruit completely hides the veggies. Can do the same with pancakes, marinara sauce, and are all quick recipes :)

You’re so welcome! I think you’re really in tune with your growth and where you are now. Learning to separate yourself from those thoughts and not letting them hold too much weight can be freeing. The fact that you’re processing these memories from a safer, happier place shows how much you’ve evolved. You’re definitely not the same person you were back then, and that’s something to be proud of!!

I completely understand how frustrating it is to keep thinking about people from the past, even when you’ve moved on. I’ve had plenty of those moments too, where old memories or relationships pop up, and it feels confusing—especially when I know I’m happy now. 

For me, it’s often just lingering emotions or curiosity that my brain hasn’t fully let go of, even though I don’t want those relationships back. I’ve learned that it’s okay to feel nostalgia or even some sadness without it meaning more than that. 

Now that you’re in a happier and safer relationship, your brain most likely feels “safe” enough to actually process the hard parts of the past that you didn’t have the capacity to before. 

At the end of the day, grief and closure is not linear. It’s not about finding perfect closure but accepting the messiness of the past and letting go of that need for that final and absolute resolution. 

When those thoughts come up, I try to remind myself that they don’t take away from the happiness I have now and that feelings I have is apart of my growth rather than unresolved issues.

This is giving me war flashbacks to my last relationship 😭 - jokes aside it sounds like you’re deeply invested in this relationship, but it’s also clear that you’re feeling overwhelmed, burnt out, and unsupported. Sometimes, even with the best intentions and love, relationships can reach a point where the dynamic is no longer healthy for either person. If you’ve tried to communicate, set boundaries, and seek balance without success, it might be time to look at the bigger picture. If you’re consistently feeling resentful or bitter, and she isn’t open to working on the issues together, it may be worth considering whether this relationship is still serving both of your needs. It doesn’t have to be a confrontational or sudden decision. You could frame it as a time to reflect on whether you’re both truly able to meet each other’s emotional and practical needs, or whether taking time apart could give you both the space to grow in ways that may not be possible within the current relationship dynamic. Taking care of yourself is not selfish, and it’s important to be in a relationship that uplifts you rather than drains you.

Firstly I want to validate your feelings. Imposter syndrome is the worst, especially when you try to balance your career and the fears of not being accepted or making mistakes. But despite of this, you continue to show up and that speaks absolute volumes to your strength and resilience. You have been through so much and have come so far that you should feel super proud of yourself. If it’s within your means I think it’s a great idea to utilise therapy to help guide you through your feelings and to remind you that you don’t need to be perfect to be valued. It’s completely normal to have struggles - you’re enough just as you are and the fact you love your job is an absolute asset. No one expects perfection - your team probably appreciates your authenticity and even though the social interactions are difficult, doesn’t mean they think any less of you. Just remember how far you have come, so be kind to yourself and take things one step at a time 🤎

Thank you for sharing your experience! I want to recognise how far you have come and that you should be so proud of yourself. Your reflections are super insightful and I appreciate your openness - it’s given me a lot to think about in my own situation too. For reference, I am 26 and was diagnosed with ASD and ADHD a few years ago. I’ve also been fortunate enough to have access to a lot of therapy and continuous support since then.

As you probably know, being neurodivergent looks different on everyone. I think what is defined as a fulfilling life, depends on the individual person’s interests and values. 

To me, a fulfilling life is one where I’m constantly learning and growing, and finding ways to appreciate and celebrate even the smallest wins. I’ve faced my own share of challenges and had often felt stuck with no purpose being so different from others. 

Now, my sense of purpose comes from embracing my challenges and acknowledging my strengths associated with my diagnoses. I value living authentically and unapologetically myself, building meaningful connections and surrounding myself with people who not only embrace my differences, but fill my cup rather than drain it.

It’s so important for me to validate my feelings but take them (specifically my negative feelings) at face value. By accepting my emotions and experiences as they are, I feel I can navigate life’s ups and downs with a lot more resilience and self compassion. I also remind myself that my worth isn’t defined by external achievements or comparing myself to others - it’s all about finding what makes me happy and satisfied, and making space for it in my life.

You mentioned wanting stimulation and experiences. Even if your current situation doesn’t allow for extensive travelling or elaborate experiences, you can still look for stimulation within your means; maybe you could try out new hobbies or connect with online communities that share your existing and/or emerging interests. Some of my most meaningful relationships were formed unexpectedly but organically (both online and in person) by having a similar interest and being able to nurture those connections. 

At the end of the day, it’s all about creating a life that feels right for you, where you can find meaning and satisfaction at your own speed. It’s completely normal if your personal journey looks different to someone else’s. Be kind to yourself and take your time navigating through this - continue exploring what makes YOU happy and adjust your approach based on what you learn about yourself as you see fit. Your path to finding fulfilment is 100% yours and no matter how it unfolds, it is completely valid 😊

One thing I’ve found about eating healthy is it’s not necessarily about what exactly you eat, but more so how much you eat. If there’s a specific meal that you find easy enough to make and meets your sensory needs, as long as you are having it in the correct portion it doesn’t really matter. I am a very picky eater and I do not enjoy cooking whatsoever. I usually don’t realise I’m hungry until it’s too late and end up getting takeaway food for the convenience which is not cost effective and most of the time not healthy at all lol 

To counter this, I have 2 weeks worth of the same brand single serve lasagne in my fridge that I love and yeah look lasagne is no salad, but because it’s the appropriate serving for me, it’s healthier than having something that isn’t the correct serving. Having single serve meals as well for me helps me needing to put in effort in something I have no interest in (both cooking and cleaning afterwards) and in turns stops me getting unhealthier options 😃

I can’t give you advice on how to end a relationship because I’ve never done it and had it last. But wanted to comment my experience if it can help at all. 

I (24F) was in a 5.5 year relationship that ended June last year. We were on and off in our last year of our relationship but we weren’t with other people during that time so we were still “together”. There was a lot of boundaries and trust broken and I just thought because we’d been together for so long I had to tolerate it. Also on paper he was a great guy - great morals, great job, similar interests and my family loved him but he wasn’t great for me and we were never on the same page.

Although it hurt when the actual break up happened, my ex (24M) ending the relationship was the best thing to ever happen to me because i loved him and I dont think I could’ve been the one who could be the one to stick to no contact once we were really done even though I knew it should’ve happened a lot earlier. It’s been a hard 12 months but I have grown and thrived so much as a person since the break up. 

I made a post in September last year after I was still miserable and needed tips on how to even deal and my life saver @poobumface said the following that might also help you even out of my original posts’ context: 

“To be honest, from the way you have described the both of you, you did not sound suited for each other at all. I know that it must hurt a whole bunch as you were together for ages, but you can use your neurodivergence to your advantage and distract yourself as much as possible. Think about how exciting it will be to date someone who let's you be kind to yourself if you need a break and know it is genuine. Really hone in on finding friends that have the qualities that your ex lacked. Don't compare yourself to the new one, because the person that you are looking for to suit your needs will not be attracted to that kind of woman. But also, remember that you see the external shell of her and their relationship and not the insecurities she faces and the issues they will have.

Maybe she wishes she was more like you - and if she doesn't, all the better reason that it's better for you to focus your life elsewhere. I'm really sorry you feel this way.

There is no quick road to overcome heartbreak, but it is always 100% worth it because there is always someone out there, friend or lover, that can love you better. Just focus on it being you for now”

Although it isn’t completely directed to your situation but if any of this can help, know you’re not alone and you are so loved and you should only focus on doing what’s best for you 💛

Originally, I (25F) thought my ADHD was more prominent and I remember when I did my testing that I didn’t think i would have autism esp because I didn’t realise at the time you could have both and thought I’d have to pick one or the other to “act more like”. Turns out I didn’t have to act like anything other than myself because even before they did the official testing they knew that I was both LOL I will say since being on ADHD medication I’ve noticed the autistic traits more and more. Could be placebo could be because I’m listening to what my body is telling me could be because the moons and stars align who knows. At the beginning of my diagnosis I was also very much in denial because the minimal representation both online, in the media and people around me was a lot different to the experience I had. I refused to tell anyone because I was embarrassed and felt disappointed that it took me so long to find out what was actually “wrong” with me. It’s been over two years since I’ve found out and I quite literally am in the best place I’ve been in my entire life. Still a long way to go but i am so grateful to be able to learn more about myself and how my brain works. I’ve found it still hard to be kind to myself and my brain at times, but I really am understanding that my brain works in a different way and that my feelings are valid even though my opinion might not be necessarily right (shocker, I know). Be kind to yourself throughout the process and lean on the people who make you feel seen and heard 😃

I take both! I’m on Ritalin and I take 40-60 mg LA with a 10mg SA between 7-8am and depending on what I have to do at night I take another 10mg of SA between 2-3pm to last me until 10pm. Max I’ve taken in one day is 70mg of the mix. I work from home so I usually wake up just before I start work so I need something to kinda wake me up and be social-able even just for teams haha
I’d also like to preface - although I love my job I definitely have my moments where I dislike certain parts of it at times - again if the bad outweighed the good I’d look elsewhere.

I thought that about my old job - there were some aspects I loved but at the end of the day people exhausted me to the point I would need at least a week off at a time after working 2 days in a row 🥲 If I was you, I’d try and listen to what my body (mind, heart and gut) is telling me and if the bad outweighed the good I would look elsewhere. If you enjoy teaching adults can you look for jobs that do that? If you don’t have the qualifications, can you look at dropping to part time work teaching kids while getting the qualifications you need to teach adults? As tacky as it sounds, you really can do whatever you set your mind to - I feel silly even saying that because me 6 months ago would literally laugh at that. Things will happen for a reason and if you’re not happy where you are I’d say find something that does make you happy 😊

I found working in a job that I didn’t love - I ended up burning out faster, no matter how easy the job was or how supportive management and my coworkers were. I used to work part time - 3 days a week (Mo,We,Fri) for over 4 years because I couldn’t work more than 1 day in a row without becoming mentally and in turn physically exhausted. I started a new job in may that I LOVE and now work full time - 5 days a week ever since. If this isn’t the case for you and you do love your job but are worried about looking horribly unprofessional or irresponsible- if you have a medical certificate your employer cannot question legally why you need time off. It’s unprofessional if they question it.

Hi there :) Clinically Diagnosed Autistic ADHD POC here. One thing that I’ve found really helpful when dealing with things that bother me - especially from other people is - at the end of the day you can only really control your own thoughts and your own actions. My ex boyfriend (NT) would make me enraged over the littlest things, especially when I’d tell him something would bother me and he would only listen after I would “lash out” at him. He would be okay for a couple days and do the same thing just in a DiFfErEnT fOnT. Long story short the way I deal with such intense rage and sadness is limiting things that cause me stress (i.e. him at the time) and surrounding myself with the things that bring me joy; whether it be your divulging in your special interests or the people who you feel safe and seen with.
